query: For high-entropy alloys intended for harsh corrosive mechanical environments, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion, and why? Propose a controlled comparison that would test the hypothesis, predict how combined degradation and its wear and corrosion components would differ from a matched baseline, define where the prediction should hold or fail, identify supporting prior evidence, and state an observation that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The ability of a high‐entropy alloy to form and continuously regenerate a stable, adherent passive oxide film under sliding contact governs its resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion; alloys with more robust film‐forming elements sustain lower tribocorrosion loss by preventing metal contact and limiting anodic dissolution.
generation.material_initial_state: Two equiatomic HEA compositions of equal hardness (~4 GPa): (1) Al–Ti–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA designed for strong Al/Ti‐rich oxide formation, (2) Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni HEA lacking strong film‐forming Al/Ti but matched for mechanical properties.
generation.intervention: Reciprocating sliding wear tests in a chloride‐containing aqueous environment under identical load and speed.
generation.conditions: 1 N normal load, 10 mm/s sliding speed, 5 000 cycles, 0.1 M NaCl solution at pH 7, 25 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Continuous formation and repair of the passive oxide layer in the wear track region.
generation.mechanism: Under mechanical film removal, the film‐forming HEA rapidly repassivates, sustaining a protective barrier that lowers friction, minimizes fresh metal exposure, and reduces anodic current; the non‐forming HEA cannot replenish its film as effectively, leading to higher corrosion–wear synergy.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Al–Ti–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA will exhibit ≈50% lower combined material loss (wear + corrosion) and ≈40% lower steady‐state corrosion current under sliding than the Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni baseline; the combined loss for the film-forming HEA will be less than the sum of its isolated wear and corrosion rates (antagonistic interaction).
generation.baseline: Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni HEA with comparable hardness but no strong Al/Ti oxide‐forming elements.
generation.boundary: At loads above ~5 N or in environments outside pH 6–8 where repassivation kinetics slow drastically, the protective effect diminishes and the hypothesis may fail.
generation.uncertainty: Estimated reduction in combined loss is approximate (30–70% based on oxide kinetics); exact values may vary with solution chemistry and microstructural state.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform identical reciprocating wear–corrosion tests (as above) on both HEAs while monitoring electrochemical current and measuring mass/wear track depth loss.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al–Ti–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA shows equal or greater combined material loss or corrosion current under sliding than the Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni baseline, or if its combined loss exceeds the sum of its isolated wear and corrosion rates by more than 10%, the hypothesis is falsified.
